title: 1　问题的界定：艺术人类学的必要性
originalTitle: 1　The Problem Defined: The Need for an Anthropology of Art

zh: 1.1　能否有一种视觉艺术的人类学理论？
en: 1.1　Can there be an Anthropological Theory of Visual Art?

zh: 一种“视觉艺术的人类学理论”大概会让人想到这样一种理论：它处理人类学家通常研究的殖民与后殖民社会中的艺术生产，外加博物馆藏品中所谓的“原始”艺术——如今通常称为“民族志”艺术。于是“艺术的人类学理论”就等于把“艺术理论”应用于“人类学的”艺术。但这并非我所设想的东西。殖民与后殖民边缘地带的艺术，只要它是“艺术”，就可以经由现有的任何一种或所有“艺术理论”来加以处理，只要这些进路是有用的。批评家、哲学家与美学家早已忙碌多时；“艺术理论”构成了一个庞大而根基深厚的领域。那些以描述和理解毕加索与布朗库西的艺术为业的人，可以把非洲面具作为“艺术”来论述，而且确实有必要这样做，因为非洲艺术与20世纪西方艺术之间存在着极为显著的艺术史关联。为我们自己的艺术发展一套“艺术理论”，又为那些曾在某个时候落入殖民主义支配之下的文化的艺术发展另一套截然不同的理论，这是没有道理的。如果西方（审美的）艺术理论适用于“我们的”艺术，那么它们就适用于所有人的艺术，并且应当如此应用。
en: An ‘anthropological theory of visual art' probably suggests a theory dealing with the art production in the colonial and post-colonial societies anthropologists typically study, plus the so-called ‘Primitive' art-now usually called ‘ethnographic' art-in museum collections. The ‘anthropological theory of art' equals the ‘theory of art' applied to ‘anthropological' art. But this is not what I have in mind. The art of the colonial and post-colonial margins, inasmuch as it is ‘art', can be approached via any, or all, of the existing ‘theories of art', in so far as these approaches are useful ones. Critics, philosophers, and aestheticians have been busy for a long time; ‘theories of art' constitute a vast and well-established field. Those whose profession it is to describe and understand the art of Picasso and Brancusi can write about masks from Africa as ‘art', and indeed need to do so because of the very salient art-historical relationships between the art of Africa and twentieth-century Western art. There is no sense in developing one ‘theory of art' for our own art, and another, distinctively different theory, for the art of those cultures who happened, once upon a time, to fall under the sway of colonialism. If Western (aesthetic) theories of art apply to ‘our' art, then they apply to everybody's art, and should be so applied.

zh: 萨莉·普赖斯（1989）有理由批评所谓“原始”艺术被本质化，继而被隔离到一个专门的领域。她主张，这种艺术理应受到西方观者以我们评价自身艺术的同一批评标准来评价。来自非西方文化的艺术在本质上并不异于我们自己的艺术，因为它是由各具才华与想象力的艺术家个人创造的，这些艺术家理应获得与西方艺术家同等程度的承认，而不应被要么视为“本能的”自然之子、自发地表达其原始冲动，要么视为某种僵化的“部落”风格的奴性演绎者。与其他当代论及民族志艺术的作者（Coote 1992, 1996; Morphy 1994, 1996）一样，普赖斯相信每种文化都有一种特定于该文化的审美，而艺术人类学的任务就是界定每种文化内在审美的特征，以便特定非西方艺术家的审美贡献能够得到正确评价，也就是相对于他们特定于文化的审美意图来评价。下面是她的信条：
en: Sally Price (1989) has rightly complained about the essentialization and concomitant ghettoization of so-called ‘Primitive' art. She argues that this art deserves to be evaluated by Western spectators according to the same critical standards we apply to our own art. Art from non-Western cultures is not essentially different from our own, in that it is produced by individual, talented, imaginative artists, who ought to be accorded the same degree of recognition as Western artists, rather than being viewed either as ‘instinctive' children of nature, spontaneously expressing their primitive urges, or, alternatively, as slavish exponents of some rigid ‘tribal' style. Like other contemporary writers on the subject of ethnographic arts (Coote 1992, 1996; Morphy 1994, 1996), Price believes that each culture has a culture-specific aesthetic, and the task of the anthropology of art is to define the characteristics of each culture's inherent aesthetic, so that the aesthetic contributions of particular non-Western artists can be evaluated correctly, that is, in relation to their culturally specific aesthetic intentions. Here is her credo:

zh: 依我看来，问题的关键在于，对原始艺术的欣赏几乎总是被表述为一种错误的两难选择：一个选项是以某种未加界定的普遍美概念为基础，让具有审美鉴别力的眼睛作我们的向导；另一个选项是埋头于“部落知识”，去发现相关对象的实用或仪式功能。这两条路径通常被视为相互竞争、互不相容……我要提出第三种构想的可能性，它居于这两个极端之间的某处……它要求接受两条信条，而这两条信条迄今尚未在西方社会的受教育成员中获得广泛接受。
en: The crux of the problem, as I understand it, is that the appreciation of Primitive Art has nearly always been phrased in terms of a fallacious choice: one option is to let the aesthetically discriminating eye be our guide on the basis of some undefined concept of universal beauty. The other is to bury ourselves in ‘tribal lore' to discover the utilitarian or ritual function of the objects in question. These two routes are generally viewed as competitive and incompatible ... I would propose the possibility of a third conceptualization that sits somewhere between the two extremes ... It requires the acceptance of two tenets that do not as yet enjoy widespread acceptance among educated members of Western societies.

zh: ——一条信条是，即便最具天赋的鉴赏家，其“眼睛”也不是赤裸的，而是透过西方文化教育的透镜来观看艺术。
en: —One tenet is that the ‘eye' of even the most naturally gifted connoisseur is not naked, but views art through the lense of a Western cultural education.

zh: ——第二条是，许多原始人（包括艺术家与批评家）同样赋有具鉴别力的“眼睛”——同样装配着一副反映其自身文化教育的光学装置。
en: —The second is that many Primitives (including both artists and critics) are also endowed with a discriminating ‘eye'-similarly fitted with an optical device that reflects their own cultural education.

zh: 在这两条信条的框架内，人类学的语境化所代表的，并非一种与真正的“审美经验”相竞争的、对异族习俗的繁琐铺陈，而是一种把审美经验扩展到我们自身狭隘的、受文化束缚的视域之外的手段。既然已经接受原始艺术作品足以与我们社会最杰出艺术家的作品并列呈现……我们接下来的任务就是承认它们得以被生产出来的那些审美框架的存在与正当性。（Price 1989: 92-3）
en: In the framework of these two tenets, anthropological contextualization represents, not a tedious elaboration of exotic customs that competes with true ‘aesthetic experience,' but rather a means to expand the aesthetic experience beyond our own narrowly culture-bound line of vision. Having accepted works of Primitive Art as worthy of representation alongside the works of our own societies' most distinguished artists ... our next task is to acknowledge the existence and legitimacy of the aesthetic frameworks within which they were produced. (Price 1989: 92-3)

zh: 这一观点与西方艺术史和艺术理论之间的密切关系完全一致。“特定文化的审美”与“特定时代的审美”之间存在着明显的类比。巴克森德尔（1972）等艺术理论家已经表明，西方艺术史上特定时期艺术的接受，取决于当时艺术是如何被“观看”的，而“观看方式”会随时间变化。要欣赏某一时期的艺术，我们应当努力重新捕捉那个时期的艺术家所默认的、公众看待其作品时会采用的“观看方式”。艺术史家的任务之一，就是通过引证历史语境来协助这一过程。人们完全可以合理地得出结论：艺术人类学有着大致相似的目标，只不过有待阐明的是一个文化系统而非一个历史时代的“观看方式”。
en: This view is perfectly consistent with the close relationship between art history and the theory of art in the West. There is an obvious analogy between ‘culture-specific aesthetics' and ‘period-specific aesthetics'. Art theorists such as Baxendall (1972) have shown that the reception of the art of particular periods in the history of Western art was dependent on how the art was ‘seen' at the time, and that ‘ways of seeing' change over time. To appreciate the art of a particular period we should try to recapture the ‘way of seeing' which artists of the period implicitly assumed their public would bring to their work. One of the art historian's tasks is to assist in this process by adducing the historical context. The anthropology of art, one might quite reasonably conclude, has an approximately similar objective, except that it is the ‘way of seeing' of a cultural system, rather than a historical period, which has to be elucidated.

zh: 就增加给予非西方艺术及艺术家的承认而言，我对普赖斯的建议并无异议。的确，除了那些“鉴赏家”——他们从这样一种想象中获得反动的满足：他们喜欢收藏的“原始艺术”的制作者是刚从树上下来的原始野蛮人——之外，哪个善意的人会反对这样一个方案呢？这些蠢人可以不予理会。
en: I have no objection to Price's suggestions so far as increasing the recognition afforded to non-Western art and artists is concerned. Indeed what wellintentioned person could object to such a programme, except possibly the ‘connoisseurs', who derive a reactionary satisfaction from imagining that the producers of the ‘primitive art' they like to collect are primeval savages, barely descended from the trees. These idiots can be dismissed out of hand.

zh: 尽管如此，我并不认为阐明非西方审美体系就构成了一种艺术的“人类学”。首先，这样一个方案纯粹是文化性的，而非社会性的。在我看来，人类学是一门社会科学学科，而非人文学科。我承认这一区分难以捉摸，但它确实意味着“艺术人类学”聚焦于艺术生产、流通与接受的社会语境，而非对特定艺术品的评价——在我看来后者是批评家的职能。例如，知道约鲁巴人为何认为一件雕刻在审美上优于另一件（R. F. Thompson 1973）也许有趣，但那并不能告诉我们多少关于约鲁巴人为何要从事雕刻的信息。在某一时期的约鲁巴地区存在大量雕刻、雕刻匠与雕刻批评家，这是一个社会事实，其解释不在本土美学的领域之内。同样，我们的审美偏好本身并不能解释那些被我们汇集于博物馆并加以审美看待的对象的存在。审美判断只是内在的心理行为；而艺术对象则是在外部物理与社会世界中被生产和流通的。这种生产与流通必须由某些具有客观性质的社会过程来维持，而这些过程又与其他社会过程（交换、政治、宗教、亲属制度等）相联系。例如，除非西非存在波罗与桑德之类的秘密会社，否则就不会有波罗与桑德面具。波罗与桑德面具之所以能够被我们或本土艺术公众加以审美看待与评价，仅仅是因为该地区存在某些社会制度。即便人们承认每种文化的观念体系中都存在某种类似于“美学”的东西作为其特征，也远未拥有一种能够解释特定艺术品在特定社会环境中生产与流通的理论。事实上，正如我在别处（Gell 1995）所论证的，我远未确信每种“文化”的观念体系中都有一个可与我们的“美学”相比拟的组成部分。我认为，想要审美地看待其他文化艺术的欲望，更多地告诉了我们关于我们自己的意识形态及其把艺术对象作为审美护符加以准宗教式崇拜的信息，而非关于这些其他文化的信息。“本土美学”的方案本质上旨在通过提供一个文化语境——非西方艺术对象可在其中被纳入西方艺术鉴赏的审美范畴——来精炼和扩展西方艺术公众的审美感受力。这本身并非坏事，但它仍远未成为一种关于艺术生产与流通的人类学理论。
en: All the same, I do not think that the elucidation of non-western aesthetic systems constitutes an ‘anthropology' of art. Firstly, such a programme is exclusively cultural, rather than social. Anthropology, from my point of view, is a social science discipline, not a humanity. The distinction is, I admit, elusive, but it does imply that the ‘anthropology of art' focuses on the social context of art production, circulation, and reception, rather than the evaluation of particular works of art, which, to my mind, is the function of a critic. It may be interesting to know why, for example, the Yoruba evaluate one carving as aesthetically superior to another (R. F. Thompson 1973), but that does not tell us much about why the Yoruba carve to begin with. The presence of large numbers of carvings, carvers, and critics of carvings in Yorubaland at a certain period in time is a social fact whose explanation does not lie in the domain of indigenous aesthetics. Similarly, our aesthetic preferences cannot by themselves account for the existence of the objects which we assemble in museums and regard aesthetically. Aesthetic judgements are only interior mental acts; art objects, on the other hand, are produced and circulated in the external physical and social world. This production and circulation has to be sustained by certain social processes of an objective kind, which are connected to other social processes (exchange, politics, religion, kinship, etc.). Unless, for instance, there were secret societies such as Poro and Sande in West Africa, there would be no Poro and Sande masks. Poro and Sande masks can be regarded and evaluated aesthetically, by ourselves, or by the indigenous art public, only because of the presence of certain social institutions in that region. Even if one were to concede that something akin to ‘aesthetics' exists as a feature of the ideational system of every culture, one would be far from possessing a theory which could account for the production and circulation of particular works of art in particular social milieux. In fact, as I have argued elsewhere (Gell 1995), I am far from convinced that every ‘culture' has a component of its ideational system which is comparable to our own ‘aesthetics'. I think that the desire to see the art of other cultures aesthetically tells us more about our own ideology and its quasi-religious veneration of art objects as aesthetic talismans, than it does about these other cultures. The project of ‘indigenous aesthetics' is essentially geared to refining and expanding the aesthetic sensitivities of the Western art public by providing a cultural context within which non-Western art objects can be assimilated to the categories of Western aesthetic art-appreciation. This is not a bad thing in itself, but it still falls far short of being an anthropological theory of art production and circulation.

zh: 我这样说是出于一些理由，这些理由不受我关于“美学”不可能用作文化描述与比较的普遍参数这一观点正确与否的影响。即便如普赖斯、库特、莫菲等人所设想的那样，所有文化都有一种“审美”，对其他文化审美的描述性说明也加起来构不成一种人类学理论。真正“人类学的”理论具有某些界定性特征，而这些关于评价图式的说明恰恰缺乏这些特征。无论何种评价图式，只有在它们于社会互动过程中发挥作用——它们正是经由这些过程而被生成和维持——的限度内，才具有人类学意义。例如，法律人类学不是研究法律—伦理原则（其他民族的是非观念），而是研究争端及其解决，争端双方在过程中确实常常诉诸这类原则。同样，艺术人类学不能是研究这种或那种文化的审美原则，而是研究审美原则（或类似之物）在社会互动过程中的调动。审美的艺术理论在任何显著方面都不类似于任何现有的关于社会过程的人类学理论。它所类似的是现有的西方艺术理论——它当然就是西方艺术理论，只不过不再应用于“西方”艺术，而是应用于异族或大众艺术。要发展一种真正人类学的艺术理论，仅仅“借用”现有艺术理论并把它应用于一个新对象是不够的；必须从现有的人类学理论发展出一个新变体，并把它应用于艺术。这并不是说我想比那些把现有艺术理论应用于异族对象的同事更有原创性，我只是想以一种新的方式做到不原创。“现有的人类学理论”不是关于艺术的；它们是关于亲属制度、生计经济、性别、宗教之类主题的。因此，目标是创造一种关于艺术的理论，它之所以是人类学的，是因为它类似于那些我们可以有信心地称为人类学的其他理论。当然，这种模仿策略在很大程度上取决于一个人把人类学视为何种学科，以及这门学科如何区别于相邻学科。
en: I say this for reasons that are unaffected by the correctness or otherwise of my views about the impossibility of using ‘aesthetics' as a universal parameter of cultural description and comparison. Even if, as Price, Coote, Morphy, and others suppose, all cultures have an ‘aesthetic', descriptive accounts of other cultures' aesthetics would not add up to an anthropological theory. Distinctively ‘anthropological' theories have certain defining characteristics, which these accounts of evaluative schemes would lack. Evaluative schemes, of whatever kind, are only of anthropological interest in so far as they play a part within social processes of interaction, through which they are generated and sustained. The anthropology of law, for instance, is not the study of legal-ethical principles -other peoples' ideas of right and wrong--but of disputes and their resolution, in the course of which disputants do often appeal to such principles. Similarly, the anthropology of art cannot be the study of the aesthetic principles of this or that culture, but of the mobilization of aesthetic principles (or something like them) in the course of social interaction. The aesthetic theory of art just does not resemble, in any salient respect, any existing anthropological theory about social processes. What it resembles is existing Western art theory-which of course it is, applied no longer to ‘Western' art, but to exotic or popular art. To develop a distinctively anthropological theory of art it is insufficient to ‘borrow' existing art theory and apply it to a new object; one must develop a new variant of existing anthropological theory, and apply it to art. It is not that I want to be more original than my colleagues who have applied the existing theory of art to exotic objects, I just want to be unoriginal in a new way. ‘Existing anthropological theories' are not about art; they are about topics like kinship, subsistence economics, gender, religion, and the like. The objective, therefore, is to create a theory about art which is anthropological because it resembles these other theories that one can confidently describe as anthropological. Of course, this imitative strategy very much depends on what sort of a subject one considers anthropology to be; and how this subject differs from neighbouring ones.

zh: “人类学理论”作为一个类别，其界定性特征是什么？我又有什么根据断言，把审美评价图式整理成体系不会落入这一类目之下？我的观点是，就人类学确有某种特定研究对象而言，这一对象就是“社会关系”——各类社会系统参与者之间的关系。我承认，博厄斯与克罗伯传统中的许多人类学家（普赖斯也在其中）认为人类学的研究对象是“文化”。这一表述的问题在于，人们只有在某个具体场景中观察和记录某人的文化行为，也就是观察他们在社会互动中如何与特定的“他者”发生关系，才能发现任何人的“文化”由什么构成。文化独立于其在社会互动中的表现便不存在；即便你让某人坐下，请他“给我们讲讲你的文化”，情形也是如此——在这种情况下，所涉及的互动就是询问的人类学家与（大概相当困惑的）报导人之间的互动。
en: What constitutes the defining characteristic of ‘anthropological theories', as a class, and what grounds have I for asserting that codifying aestheticevaluative schemes would not fall under such a rubric? My view is that in so far as anthropology has a specific subject-matter at all, that subject-matter is ‘social relationships'-relationships between participants in social systems of various kinds. I recognize that many anthropologists in the tradition of Boas and Kroeber, Price among them, consider that the subject-matter of anthropology is ‘culture'. The problem with this formulation is that one only discovers what anybody's ‘culture' consists of by observing and recording their cultural behaviour in some specific setting, that is, how they relate to specific ‘others' in social interactions. Culture has no existence independently of its manifestations in social interactions; this is true even if one sits someone down and asks them to ‘tell us about your culture'-in this case the interaction in question is the one between the inquiring anthropologist and the (probably rather bemused) informant.

zh: 在我看来，“本土美学”方案的问题在于，它倾向于脱离“审美反应”表现于其中的社会语境而把这种反应实体化（而博厄斯式人类学总体上把文化实体化）。就可能存在一种“美学”的人类学理论而言，这样一种理论会试图解释社会施动者在特定场景中为何会以特定方式回应特定艺术品。我认为这可以与一项值得称道但本质上非人类学的任务区分开来，即为非西方艺术提供一个“语境”，使这种艺术能够为西方艺术公众所接近。然而，本土艺术“公众”对本土艺术的反应，远非枚举那些在“欣赏”艺术时动用某种审美评价图式的语境所能穷尽。这类语境可能稀少甚至不存在，但“在我们看来像艺术的东西”仍然被生产和流通着。
en: The problem with the ‘indigenous aesthetics' programme, in my view, is that it tends to reify the ‘aesthetic response' independently of the social context of its manifestations (and that Boasian anthropology in general reifies culture). In so far as there can be an anthropological theory of ‘aesthetics', such a theory would try to explain why social agents, in particular settings, produce the responses that they do to particular works of art. I think that this can be distinguished from the laudable, but essentially non-anthropological task of providing a ‘context' for non-Western art such that this art can become accessible to a Western art-public. However, the responses of the indigenous art ‘public' to indigenous art is hardly exhausted by the enumeration of those contexts in which something like an evaluative aesthetic scheme is deployed in ‘appreciating' art. Such contexts may be rare or non-existent, yet ‘what looks to us like art' is none the less produced and circulated.

zh: 一种纯粹文化性的、审美的、“欣赏式的”艺术对象进路是人类学的死胡同。相反，令我感兴趣的问题是：鉴于人类学理论首先作为关于社会关系的理论而非别的什么而“可被识别”这一前提，建构一种自然契合人类学语境的“艺术理论”是否可能。设想这一点的最简单方式，是假定可能存在这样一种人类学理论：在其中，人或“社会施动者”在某些语境中被艺术对象所替代。
en: A purely cultural, aesthetic, ‘appreciative' approach to art objects is an anthropological dead end. Instead, the question which interests me is the possibility of formulating a ‘theory of art' which fits naturally into the context of anthropology, given the premiss that anthropological theories are 'recognizable' initially, as theories about social relationships, and not anything else. The simplest way to imagine this is to suppose that there could be a species of anthropological theory in which persons or ‘social agents' are, in certain contexts, substituted for by art objects.

zh: 1.2　艺术对象
en: 1.2　The Art Object

zh: 这立即引出了“艺术对象”的定义问题，乃至“艺术”本身的定义问题。霍华德·莫菲（1994: 648-85）在最近一篇讨论人类学语境中“艺术定义”问题的文章里，考虑并拒绝了（西方的）艺术制度定义，即“艺术”就是由获得制度承认的艺术界成员（Danto 1964）——批评家、画商、收藏家、理论家等——当作艺术来对待的任何东西。这相当公允：人类学家所关注的许多社会并无“艺术界”可言，然而这些社会却生产出一些被我们的“艺术界”承认为“艺术”的作品。按照“艺术制度论”，大多数本土艺术之所以是“艺术”（在我们用“艺术”一词所指的意义上），只是因为我们认为它是，而非因为制作它的人这样认为。接受艺术界的艺术定义，就迫使人类学家把一种带有明显都会性质的参照框架强加于其他文化的艺术。这在某种程度上不可避免（人类学是一种都会活动，正如艺术批评一样），但莫菲不愿接受（在人类学上无知的）西方艺术界关于西方的地理边界之外“艺术”定义的裁断，这是可以理解的。他转而提出一个二元定义：艺术对象是那些“具有用于呈现或再现目的的语义和/或审美属性的对象”（同上，655），也就是说，艺术对象要么是传达“意义”的符号载体，要么是为激起一种文化上认可的审美反应而制作的对象，要么同时是这两者。
en: This immediately raises the question of the definition of the ‘art object', and indeed, of ‘art' itself. Howard Morphy (1994: 648-85) in a recent discussion of the problem of the ‘definition of art' in the anthropological context, considers, and rejects, the (Western) institutional definition of art, that ‘art' is whatever is treated as art by members of the institutionally recognized art world (Danto 1964)-critics, dealers, collectors, theoreticians, etc. This is fair enough: there is no ‘art world' to speak of in many of the societies which anthropologists concern themselves with, yet these societies produce works some of which are recognized as ‘art' by our ‘art world'. According to the ‘institutional theory of art', most indigenous art is only ‘art' (in the sense we mean by ‘art') because we think it is, not because the people who make it think so. Accepting the art world's definition of art obliges the anthropologist to bring to bear on the art of other cultures a frame of reference of an overtly metropolitan character. To some extent this is inevitable (anthropology is a metropolitan activity, just like art criticism) but Morphy is understandably disinclined to accept the verdict of the (anthropologically uninformed) Western art world as to the definition of ‘art' beyond the physical frontiers of the West. He proposes, instead, a dualistic definition; art objects are those ‘having semantic and/or aesthetic properties that are used for presentational or representational purposes' (ibid. 655), that is, either art objects are sign-vehicles, conveying ‘meaning', or they are objects made in order to provoke a culturally endorsed aesthetic response, or both of these simultaneously.

zh: 我认为艺术对象身份的这两个条件都成问题。我已经表达过这样的看法：从人类学上说，人们在特定社会场景中使用可能被称为“艺术对象”的事物，不能脱离这一使用所涉及的社会过程来考察其“审美属性”。例如，我怀疑战场上的战士会“审美地”关注敌方战士盾牌上的图案；然而图案被置于其上，恰恰是为了被这个战士看到（并吓到他）。这面盾牌，如果它像卷首插图（第xxiv页）那面一样，就无可争议地是一件令人类学家感兴趣的那类艺术品，但它的审美属性（对我们而言）与它的人类学意涵完全无关。从人类学上说，它不是一面“美的”盾牌，而是一面引发恐惧的盾牌。在社会生活展开的图景中，对人工制品的社会/情绪反应有无数层次（恐惧、欲望、敬畏、着迷等），不能用审美感受来概括，也不能还原为审美感受；除非把审美反应泛化到完全无意义的地步。反应理论“审美化”的效果，无非是尽可能把民族志他者的反应等同于我们自己的反应。事实上，对人工制品的反应从来不会从种种可接触的人工制品中，单独挑出那些被“审美地”关注的和那些不被如此关注的。
en: I find both of these conditions for art object status questionable. I have already expressed the opinion that ‘aesthetic properties' cannot be abstracted, anthropologically, from the social processes surrounding the deployment of candidate ‘art objects' in specific social settings. I doubt, for example, that a warrior on a battlefield is ‘aesthetically' interested in the design on an opposing warrior's shield; yet it was so as to be seen by this warrior (and to frighten him) that the design was placed there. The shield, if it resembles the one in the frontispiece (p. xxiv), is indisputably a work of art of the kind interesting to the anthropologist, but its aesthetic properties (for us) are totally irrelevant to its anthropological implications. Anthropologically, it is not a ‘beautiful' shield, but a fear-inducing shield. The innumerable shades of social/emotional responses to artefacts (of terror, desire, awe, fascination, etc.) in the unfolding patterns of social life cannot be encompassed or reduced to aesthetic feelings; not without making the aesthetic response so generalized as to be altogether meaningless. The effect of the ‘aestheticization' of response-theory is simply to equate the reactions of the ethnographic Other, as far as possible, to our own. In fact, responses to artefacts are never such as to single out, among the spectrum of available artefacts, those that are attended to ‘aesthetically' and those that are not.

zh: 我也不同意这样一种看法：艺术品之所以能被识别为一类事物，是因为它参与了一套用于传达意义的“视觉”编码。我完全拒绝这种想法，即除语言本身之外的任何东西都在这里所说的意义上具有“意义”。语言是一种独特的制度（有其生物学基础）。借助语言，我们可以谈论对象，并在“找点关于它们的话来说”的意义上把“意义”归于它们；但视觉艺术对象并不因此就是语言的一部分，也不构成一种替代性语言。视觉艺术对象是我们可能、而且通常确实会谈起的对象——但它们本身要么不说话，要么以文字编码呈现自然语言。我们使用符号谈论对象，但艺术对象除非在特殊情况下，并不是本身带有“意义”的符号；而且如果它们确有意义，那么它们是语言的一部分（即书写符号），而不是一种独立的“视觉”语言。我会不时回到这个话题，因为我对“艺术语言”观念的论战有许多不同方面，分开处理更好。眼下，让我只是提醒读者：我在全书中都避免使用“象征意义”这一概念。这种拒绝以象征符号和意义来讨论艺术的做法可能令人有些惊讶，因为许多人认为“艺术”领域与象征领域或多或少是重合的。我以能动性、意图、因果、结果与转化取代象征沟通，把全部重心放在这些之上。我把艺术视为一个行动系统，旨在改变世界，而非编码关于世界的象征命题。以“行动”为中心的艺术进路本质上比另一种符号学进路更具人类学性，因为它关注的是艺术对象在社会过程中的实际中介作用，而非把对象“仿佛”当作文本来解释。
en: Nor am I happy with the idea that the work of art is recognizable, generically, in that it participates in a ‘visual' code for the communication of meaning. I entirely reject the idea that anything, except language itself, has ‘meaning' in the intended sense. Language is a unique institution (with a biological basis). Using language, we can talk about objects and attribute ‘meanings' to them in the sense of ‘find something to say about them' but visual art objects are not part of language for this reason, nor do they constitute an alternative language. Visual art objects are objects about which we may, and commonly do, speak—but they themselves either do not speak, or they utter natural language in graphemic code. We talk about objects, using signs, but art objects are not, except in special cases, signs themselves, with ‘meanings'; and if they do have meanings, then they are part of language (i.e. graphic signs), not a separate 'visual' language. I shall return to this subject at intervals, since my polemic against the idea of a ‘language of art' has many different aspects to it, which are better dealt with separately. For the present, let me simply warn the reader that I have avoided the use of the notion of ‘symbolic meaning' throughout this work. This refusal to discuss art in terms of symbols and meanings may occasion some surprise, since the domain of ‘art' and the symbolic are held by many to be more or less coextensive. In place of symbolic communication, I place all the emphasis on agency, intention, causation, result, and transformation. I view art as a system of action, intended to change the world rather than encode symbolic propositions about it. The 'action'-centred approach to art is inherently more anthropological than the alternative semiotic approach because it is preoccupied with the practical mediatory role of art objects in the social process, rather than with the interpretation of objects ‘as if' they were texts.

zh: 既然为了艺术人类学的目的拒绝了莫菲用以区分“艺术对象”类别的两个标准，我当然仍面临着一个未解决的问题：提出一个艺术对象身份的标准。然而幸运的是，艺术人类学理论并不需要提供一种独立于理论本身的艺术对象身份标准。人类学家没有义务事先以一种令美学家、哲学家、艺术史家或任何其他人满意的方式来定义艺术对象。我所使用的艺术对象定义不是制度性的，也不是审美的或符号学的；这个定义是理论性的。艺术对象就是被插入理论所设想（稍后概述）的术语与关系系统中为艺术对象预留的“槽位”的任何东西。关于这个对象的性质，没有任何东西可以事先判定，因为该理论的前提是：艺术对象的性质是它嵌入其中的社会关系矩阵的函数。它没有独立于关系语境的“内在”性质。我实际将讨论的大多数艺术对象都是我们毫不费力就能识别为“艺术”的知名之作，例如《蒙娜丽莎》。鉴于我们承认一个前理论的艺术对象范畴——它分为“西方”艺术对象与“本土”或“民族志”艺术对象两大子类——为方便起见，我以这些范畴的“典型”成员来展开讨论。但事实上，从人类学观点看，原则上任何事物都可能成为艺术对象，包括活人，因为艺术人类学理论（我们可以粗略地把它定义为“中介社会能动性的对象周边的社会关系”）与关于人及其身体的社会人类学无缝融合。因此，从艺术人类学的观点看，神庙中被信为神之身体的偶像，与同样为神提供临时身体的灵媒，在理论上被同等对待，尽管前者是人工制品而后者是人。
en: Having rejected Morphy's two criteria for discriminating the class of ‘art objects' for the purposes of the anthropology of art, I am, of course, still left with the unsolved problem of proposing a criterion for art object status. Fortunately, however, the anthropological theory of art does not need to provide a criterion for art object status which is independent of the theory itself. The anthropologist is not obliged to define the art object, in advance, in a way satisfactory to aestheticians, or philosophers, or art historians, or anybody else. The definition of the art object I make use of is not institutional, nor is it aesthetic or semiotic; the definition is theoretical. The art object is whatever is inserted into the ‘slot' provided for art objects in the system of terms and relations envisaged in the theory (to be outlined later). Nothing is decidable in advance about the nature of this object, because the theory is premised on the idea that the nature of the art object is a function of the social-relational matrix in which it is embedded. It has no ‘intrinsic' nature, independent of the relational context. Most of the art objects I shall actually discuss are well-known ones that we have no difficulty in identifying as ‘art'; for instance, the Mona Lisa. Inasmuch as we recognize a pre-theoretical category of art objects-split into the two major subcategories of ‘Western' art objects and ‘Indigenous' or ‘Ethnographic' art objects-I conduct the discussion in terms of ‘prototypical' members of these categories, for convenience's sake. But in fact anything whatsoever could, conceivably, be an art object from the anthropological point of view, including living persons, because the anthropological theory of art (which we can roughly define as the ‘social relations in the vicinity of objects mediating social agency') merges seamlessly with the social anthropology of persons and their bodies. Thus, from the point of view of the anthropology of art, an idol in a temple believed to be the body of the divinity, and a spiritmedium, who likewise provides the divinity with a temporary body, are treated as theoretically on a par, despite the fact that the former is an artefact and the latter is a human being.

zh: 1.3　艺术社会学
en: 1.3　Art Sociology

zh: 我刚刚把“艺术人类学”临时定义为对“中介社会能动性的对象周边的社会关系”的理论研究，并提出：艺术人类学要成为真正人类学的，就必须基于这样一个立场——在相关的理论方面，艺术对象等同于人，更准确地说，等同于社会施动者。难道这一看似激进的命题就没有替代方案吗？嗯，人们或许可以从深渊边退回，同意即便艺术人类学理论不是“跨文化美学”或符号学的一个分支，它仍可以是一种艺术“制度”社会学，而不必作出艺术对象具有人格这一激进断言。的确，有一种繁荣的“艺术社会学”，恰恰关注艺术生产、接受与流通的制度参数。然而，“艺术社会学”（制度）主要关注西方艺术，或者在西方艺术之外，关注中国、日本等拥有官僚制的先进国家的艺术，这并非巧合。除非相关制度实际存在，否则不可能有一种“制度性的”艺术社会学；这些制度即艺术公众、对艺术家的公共或私人赞助、艺术批评家、艺术博物馆、学院、艺术学校等等。
en: I have just provisionally defined the ‘anthropology of art' as the theoretical study of ‘social relations in the vicinity of objects mediating social agency' and I have suggested that in order for the anthropology of art to be specifically anthropological, it has to proceed on the basis that, in relevant theoretical respects, art objects are the equivalent of persons, or more precisely, social agents. Are there no alternatives to this seemingly radical proposition? Well, one might draw back from the abyss, and agree that even if the anthropological theory of art were not to be ‘cross-cultural aesthetics' or a branch of semiotics, then it could still be a sociology of art ‘institutions' which would not necessarily involve the radical affirmation of the personhood of art objects. There is, indeed, a flourishing ‘sociology of art' which concerns itself precisely with the institutional parameters of art production, reception, and circulation. However, it is not coincidental that the ‘sociology of art' (institutions) has been primarily concerned with Western art, or, failing that, the art of advanced states with bureaucracies, such as China, Japan, etc. There cannot be an 'institutional' sociology of art unless the relevant institutions are extant; that is, an art public, public or private patronage of artists, art critics, art museums, academies, art schools, and so on.

zh: 处理艺术社会学的作者，如伯格（1972）与布迪厄（1968, 1984），关注的是大众社会的特定制度特征，而非特定互动场景中围绕特定艺术品的关系网络。这种分工是典型的；人类学更关注社会互动的直接语境及其“个人”维度，而社会学更关注制度。当然，社会学/制度视角与人类学/关系视角之间存在连续性。人类学家不能忽视制度；艺术人类学必须考虑艺术品生产与流通的制度框架，只要这类制度存在。但仍有理由说，在许多社会中，为艺术生产与流通提供语境的“制度”并不是专门的“艺术”制度本身，而是范围更一般的制度，例如祭祀崇拜、交换系统等。如果艺术人类学把自己局限于那种可在先进官僚/工业国家语境中便于研究的制度化艺术生产与流通，它就永远难以得到充分发展。
en: Writers who deal with the sociology of art, such as Berger (1972) and Bourdieu (1968, 1984), concern themselves with particular institutional characteristics of mass societies, rather than with the network of relationships surrounding particular artworks in specific interactive settings. This division of labour is characteristic; anthropology is more concerned with the immediate context of social interactions and their ‘personal' dimensions, whereas sociology is more preoccupied with institutions. Of course, there is continuity between the sociological/institutional perspective and the anthropological/relational one. Anthropologists cannot ignore institutions; the anthropology of art has to consider the institutional framework of the production and circulation of artworks, in so far as such institutions exist. But it remains true to say that there are many societies in which the ‘institutions' which provide the context for the production and circulation of art are not specialized ‘art' institutions as such, but institutions of more general scope; for example, cults, exchange systems, etc. The anthropology of art would forever remain a very undeveloped field were it to restrict itself to institutionalized art production and circulation comparable to that which can readily be studied in the context of advanced bureaucratic/industrial states.

zh: 事实上，“艺术社会学”在“艺术人类学”中主要以“民族志”艺术市场研究的形式出现，例如斯坦纳（1994）杰出的近作。莫菲（1991）、普赖斯（1989）、托马斯（1991）等人就西方艺术公众对非西方艺术的接受写得极富启发；但这些研究关注的是西方（制度化的）艺术界，以及本土人民对其艺术生产被这个外来艺术界接受所作的反应。我认为可以把这些关于非西方艺术之接受与挪用的研究，与一种真正人类学的艺术理论的范围区分开来，这绝非贬低这类研究。人们必须问：某件艺术品在制作时是否确实考虑过日后会以这种方式被接受或挪用。在当代世界，许多“民族志”艺术实际上是为都会市场生产的；在这种情况下，除了在这一特定框架内处理它之外别无他法。然而同样真实的是，在过去乃至今天，艺术曾经并且仍然为远为有限的流通而生产，独立于这种艺术可能跨越文化与制度边界所获得的任何接受。在这些地方语境中，艺术的生产并不取决于特定“艺术”制度的存在，而是社会生活中的种种中介活动以及用途更广的制度的副产品；这就证成了这样一种主张：一种不为任何特定艺术相关制度之存在所限定的艺术人类学，至少具有相对自主性。
en: As it is, the ‘sociology of art' is represented in the ‘anthropology of art' primarily in the guise of studies of the market in ‘ethnographic' art, such as the distinguished recent work by Steiner (1994). Morphy (1991), Price (1989), Thomas (1991), and others have written very illuminatingly about the reception of non-Western art by the Western art-public; but these studies concern themselves with the (institutionalized) art world of the West, and the responses by indigenous people to the reception of their artistic production by this alien art world. I think one can distinguish between these investigations of the reception and appropriation of non-Western art, and the scope of a genuinely anthropological theory of art, which is not to denigrate such studies in any way. One has to ask whether a given work of art was actually produced with this reception or appropriation in mind. In the contemporary world, much ‘ethnographic' art is actually produced for the metropolitan market; in which case there is no possible way of dealing with it except in this specific framework. However, it also remains true that in the past, and still today, art was and is produced for much more limited circulation, independently of any reception which may be accorded to this art across cultural and institutional boundaries. These local contexts, in which art is produced not as a function of the existence of specific ‘art' institutions, but as a by-product of the mediation of social life and the existence of institutions of a more general-purpose kind, justify the assertion of at least relative autonomy for an anthropology of art not circumscribed by the presence of institutions of any specific, art-related, kind.

zh: 这样看来，艺术人类学至少可以临时地与艺术制度或“艺术界”的研究区分开来。这意味着需要回到并重新考虑上面提出的命题。说艺术对象要进入一种“人类学的”艺术理论就必须被视为“人”，似乎是个怪异的念头。但只有当人们忘记人类学整个历史倾向一直是对“人”这一概念的激进陌生化与相对化时，才会如此觉得。自这门学科伊始，人类学就显著地关注一系列问题，涉及人与“物”之间表面古怪的关系——这些物以某种方式“显现为”人，或充当人。这一基本主题最初由泰勒在《原始文化》（1875）中提出，回想一下，他在书中把“万物有灵论”（即把生命与感受性归于无生命之物、植物、动物等）讨论为“原始”文化、甚至可能是一般文化的界定性属性。弗雷泽在其关于交感巫术与接触巫术的卷帙浩繁的研究中回到了完全相同的主题。同样的关注以不同方式浮现于马林诺夫斯基与莫斯的著作中，这次是相对于“交换”以及巫术这一经典人类学主题，二者也都就此大量著述。
en: It seems, then, that the anthropology of art can be at least provisionally separated from the study of art institutions or the ‘art world'. Which implies the need to return to, and reconsider, the proposition advanced above. To suggest that art objects, to figure in an ‘anthropological' theory of art, have to be considered as ‘persons', seems a bizarre notion. But only if one fails to bear in mind that the entire historical tendency of anthropology has been towards a radical defamiliarization and relativization of the notion of ‘persons'. Since the outset of the discipline, anthropology has been signally preoccupied with a series of problems to do with ostensibly peculiar relations between persons and ‘things' which somehow ‘appear as', or do duty as, persons. This basic theme was initially announced by Tylor in Primitive Culture (1875), where, it will be recalled, he discusses ‘animism' (i.e. the attribution of life and sensibility to inanimate things, plants, animals, etc.) as the defining attribute of ‘primitive' culture, if not culture in general. Frazer returns to precisely the same theme in his voluminous studies of sympathetic and contagious magic. Identical preoccupations surface, in a different way, in the work of Malinowski and Mauss, this time in relation to ‘exchange' as well as the classical anthropological theme of magic, about which each also wrote extensively.

zh: 刚刚提出的命题——艺术人类学理论就是“把艺术对象视为人”的艺术理论——我希望读者一看便知是莫斯式的。既然在莫斯式交换理论中，馈赠或“礼物”被当作人（或人的延展）来对待，那么显然就有空间以同样方式把艺术对象视为“人”。事实上，或许可以并不过分地说：就莫斯的交换理论是典范的、原型的“人类学理论”而言，产生一种“艺术人类学理论”的途径，就是建构一种类似于莫斯理论、但关于艺术对象而非馈赠的理论。列维-斯特劳斯的亲属制度理论就是把“馈赠”换成“女人”的莫斯；所提出的“艺术人类学理论”就是把“馈赠”换成“艺术对象”的莫斯。实际上，这会是对我即将提出的理论的歪曲，但我作此类比是为了引导读者了解我的基本意图。我要表达的要点是：任何给定主题的人类学理论，只有在关键方面类似于其他人类学理论的限度内才是“人类学的”，否则“人类学的”这一称谓就毫无意义。我的目标是产生一种与其他人类学理论具有亲和性的艺术人类学理论，当然不只是莫斯的理论，还有各种其他理论。我对民族志艺术的“跨文化美学”与“符号学”理论的基本反对之一在于：这些进路在理论上与（西方）美学和艺术理论相亲，与人类学自身独立发展出的理论却没有这种亲缘。也许不存在能够建立在现有人类学理论之上或从中导出的有用艺术理论，但在人们做出建构一种真正人类学的艺术理论的实验之前，这个问题无法判定。
en: The proposition just advanced, that the anthropological theory of art is the theory of art which ‘considers art objects as persons' is, I hope, immediately and legibly Maussian. Given that prestations or ‘gifts' are treated in Maussian exchange theory as (extensions of) persons, then there is obviously scope for seeing art objects as ‘persons' in the same way. In fact, it might not be going too far to suggest that in so far as Mauss's theory of exchange is the exemplary, prototypical, ‘anthropological theory' then the way to produce an ‘anthropological theory of art' would be to construct a theory which resembles Mauss's, but which was about art objects rather than prestations. Levi-Strauss's kinship theory is Mauss with ‘prestations' replaced by ‘women'; the proposed 'anthropological theory of art' would be Mauss with ‘prestations' replaced by ‘art objects'. Actually, this would be a travesty of the theory I am about to produce, but I make the analogy in order to guide the reader as to my basic intentions. The point I am making is that an anthropological theory of any given topic is only ‘anthropological' to the extent that it resembles, in key respects, other anthropological theories, otherwise the designation ‘anthropological' has no meaning. My aim is to produce an anthropological theory of art which has affinities towards other anthropological theories, not just Mauss's of course, but various others as well. One of my basic objections to the ‘cross-cultural aesthetics' and ‘semiotics' theories of ethnographic art is that the theoretical affinities of these approaches lie in (Western) aesthetics and art-theory, not autonomously within anthropology itself. It may be that there is no useful theory of art that can be founded on or derived from existing anthropological theory, but until one has made the experiment to construct a genuinely anthropological theory of art, this question cannot be decided.

zh: 1.4　一种人类学理论的轮廓
en: 1.4　The Silhouette of an Anthropological Theory

zh: 我已达到的立场是：艺术人类学理论是一种“看起来像”人类学理论的理论，其中理论所描述其关系的某些关系项是艺术品。但“人类学的”理论看起来是什么样？人们真能给出一种人类学理论区别于任何其他类型理论的、可资识别的轮廓吗？嗯，也许不能，因为人类学是一个包容广泛的领域，与社会学、历史学、社会地理学、社会与认知心理学等其他学科只有非常含糊的区分。这一点我欣然承认。另一方面，让我们从相邻学科的角度考虑人类学家最擅长做什么。直白地说，人类学被认为擅长对表面上非理性的行为、表演、话语等提供细密的分析（“我的兄弟是一只绿鹦鹉”问题：Sperber 1985; Hollis 1970）。既然几乎所有行为从某个人的观点看都是“表面上非理性的”，人类学也许有一个稳固的未来。人类学家如何解决关于人类行为表面非理性的问题？他们这样做：与其说把行为定位或语境化于“文化”（这是一个抽象），不如说定位或语境化于社会互动的动态过程之中，后者固然可能受“文化”制约，但最好被视为一个在时间中展开的真实过程或辩证过程。不言而喻，人类学对社会行为的解释视角与社会学和社会心理学共享，更不用说其他学科。人类学区别于这些学科之处在于提供一种特殊的景深，也许最好把它描述为取“生命史尺度”，也就是说，人类学看待社会施动者的视角试图复现这些施动者看待自身的时间视角，而（历史）社会学往往是超过个人生命史尺度的，社会或认知心理学的时间尺度则小于个人生命史。因此人类学倾向于聚焦于施动者“一生”——更准确地说“生命阶段”——语境中的“行动”。人类学的基本周期是生命周期。这种时间视角（遵循生命史尺度）规定了人类学家离研究对象该多近、该多远；如果人类学家以许多实验室认知心理学典型的微观尺度研究（比如说）认知，生命史视角就丧失了，人类学家实际上就是在做认知心理学；反之，如果人类学家的视角扩张到个人生命史中“生命周期”的节律不再限定论述范围的程度，他或她就是在做历史学或社会学。
en: The position I have reached is that an anthropological theory of art is one which ‘looks like' an anthropological theory, in which certain of the relata, whose relations are described in the theory, are works of art. But what do ‘anthropological' theories look like? Can one really give an identificatory silhouette of an anthropological theory as opposed to any other kind of theory? Well, possibly not, in that anthropology is a broad church and is only very ambiguously distinct from other disciplines, such as sociology, history, social geography, social and cognitive psychology, and so on. This much I readily concede. On the other hand, let us consider what anthropologists do best from the viewpoint of neighbouring disciplines. Anthropology is, to put it bluntly, considered good at providing close-grained analyses of apparently irrational behaviour, performances, utterances, etc. (The ‘my brother is a green parrot' problem: Sperber 1985; Hollis 1970.) Since almost all behaviour is, from somebody's point of view, ‘apparently irrational' anthropology has, possibly, a secure future. How do anthropologists solve problems about the apparent irrationality of human behaviour? They do so by locating, or contextualizing behaviour not so much in ‘culture' (which is an abstraction) as in the dynamics of social interaction, which may indeed be conditioned by ‘culture' but which is better seen as a real process, or dialectic, unfolding in time. The anthropological interpretative perspective on social behaviour is shared, needless to say, with sociology and social psychology, not to mention other disciplines. Anthropology differs from these in providing a particular depth of focus, which perhaps one could best describe as ‘biographical', that is, the view taken by anthropology of social agents attempts to replicate the time perspective of these agents on themselves, whereas (historical) sociology is often, so to speak, supra-biographical and social or cognitive psychology are infra-biographical. Anthropology therefore tends to focus on the ‘act' in the context of the ‘life'—or more precisely, the ‘stage of life'-of the agent. The fundamental periodicity of anthropology is the life cycle. This time perspective (fidelity to the biographical) dictates just how close to and how far away from the subject the anthropologist stands; if the anthropologist studies (say) cognition at the micro-scale typical of much laboratory cognitive psychology, the biographical perspective is lost and the anthropologist, in effect, is just doing cognitive psychology; conversely, if the anthropologist's perspective expands to the degree that the biographical ‘life cycle' rhythm no longer delimits the scope of the discourse, he or she is doing history or sociology.

zh: 也许这种人类学定义不会合所有人的意，但我要争辩说，它实际上涵盖了大多数被视为典型“人类学的”工作。这种特定于生命史尺度的景深当然也有其空间对应物；人类学的空间就是施动者在人生历程中走过的空间，无论它们是狭窄的，还是如日益常见的那样广阔乃至世界性的。此外，它还规定了某种看待社会关系的观点。人类学家通常在“生命史”语境中看待关系，我的意思是，关系被视为个人生命史上一连串关系的一部分，这些关系在生命周期的不同阶段建立。“社会学的”关系是所谓恒久的，或超出个人生命史的，如资本主义中阶级之间的关系，或等级社会中地位群体（种姓）之间的关系。另一方面，“心理学的”关系所涉的时间尺度小于个人生命史，往往不过是瞬间的“遭遇”，例如在实验场景中，被试被要求以在他们各自的生命史中既无先例、也无后果的方式彼此互动并与实验者互动。人类学的关系是真实的关系，它们对个人生命史有实际影响，并与施动者的人生“筹划”相衔接。
en: Perhaps this definition of anthropology will not be to the liking of all, but I would argue that it does in fact encompass most of the work which is regarded as typically ‘anthropological'. This specifically biographical depth of focus has of course also a spatial correlate; the spaces of anthropology are those which are traversed by agents in the course of their biographies, be they narrow, or, as is becoming increasingly the case, wide or even world-wide. Moreover, it dictates a certain view of social relations. Anthropologists typically view relationships in a ‘biographical' context, by which I mean that relationships are seen as part of a biographical series entered into at different phases of the life cycle. ‘Sociological' relations, are, so to speak, perennial, or supra-biographical, like the relation between the classes in capitalism, or the relationship between status-groups (castes) in hierarchical societies. ‘Psychological' relations, on the other hand, are infra-biographical, often no more than momentary 'encounters', as, for instance, in experimental settings in which subjects are required to interact with one another, and with the experimenter, in ways which have no biographical precedents or consequences. Anthropological relationships are real and biographically consequential ones, which articulate to the agent's biographical ‘life project'.

zh: 如果这些界定是正确的，那么一种“人类学理论”的特征轮廓就开始显现了。人类学理论的独特之处在于它们通常关于社会关系；这些关系反过来展开于一定的生命史空间，文化在其中经由一系列生命阶段被习得、转化和传递。对生命历程中的关系（文化借以获得与再生产的那些关系）的研究，以及对施动者试图通过与他人的关系来实现的人生筹划的研究，使人类学家能够完成分配给他们的智识任务，即解释人们为何会以特定方式行动，即便这种行为显得非理性、残酷，或惊人地圣洁无私。人类学理论的目标是在社会关系语境中理解行为。相应地，艺术人类学理论的目标是解释艺术对象的生产与流通如何取决于这一关系语境。
en: If these stipulations are correct, then the characteristic silhouette of an ‘anthropological theory' is beginning to emerge. Anthropological theories are distinctive in that they are typically about social relationships; these, in turn, occupy a certain biographical space, over which culture is picked up, transformed, and passed on, through a series of life-stages. The study of relationships over the life course (the relationships through which culture is acquired and reproduced) and the life-projects which agents seek to realize through their relations with others, allows anthropologists to perform their allotted intellectual task, which is to explain why people behave as they do, even if this behaviour seems irrational, or cruel, or amazingly saintly and disinterested, as may be. The aim of anthropological theory is to make sense of behaviour in the context of social relations. Correspondingly, the objective of the anthropological theory of art is to account for the production and circulation of art objects as a function of this relational context.
